AgriNova AI – NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

We are building an AI-powered agricultural decision-support solution using NASA Earth observation data.

Our goal is to help farmers compare crop rotation options by analyzing environmental conditions, climate data.

We are looking for motivated participants interested in Python, AI/ML, data science, satellite data, GIS, agriculture, and web development.

Beginners are welcome if they are willing to learn, collaborate, and contribute.
summary:
FarmFusion – Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data

FarmFusion is a research prototype developed to investigate how climate conditions and soil-water storage influence water availability for wheat cultivation in Phalia, Punjab, Pakistan. The project uses daily climate data from NASA POWER for the period 23 November 2023 to 20 April 2024. It calculates reference evapotranspiration using the FAO-56 approach, estimates wheat crop-water demand, and simulates soil-water conditions under different soil-texture and initial-moisture assumptions.

We developed an interactive Streamlit dashboard featuring climate analysis, soil-water comparisons, water-balance results, and a scenario explorer covering 36 simulated scenarios. The project addresses climate-resilient agriculture by making climate data and modeled soil-water conditions easier to explore and compare.

FarmFusion demonstrates how NASA Earth observation-related climate data can be applied to a local agricultural research problem. Its results are exploratory, and further work using measured local soil properties and field observations is needed to assess the model's accuracy.
details:
Project Details – FarmFusion

FarmFusion is an interactive agricultural water-analysis tool designed to explore how climate conditions and soil-water storage affect wheat cultivation in Phalia, Punjab, Pakistan.

How it works:
The project uses daily climate data from NASA POWER for the period 23 November 2023 to 20 April 2024. Using the FAO-56 approach, it calculates reference evapotranspiration and estimates crop-water demand for wheat. A soil-water simulation explores how different soil textures and initial soil-moisture conditions influence modeled water availability throughout the growing season. The dashboard presents 36 scenarios for comparison.

Benefits and intended impact:
FarmFusion brings climate analysis, soil-water comparisons, and water-demand results together in one interactive dashboard. It helps users explore potential water-stress conditions and understand how rainfall and soil characteristics influence agricultural water availability. Its intended impact is to support agricultural research and encourage more informed, climate-aware water-management decisions.

Tools and technologies:

  • Python: Core programming language.
  • NumPy: Numerical calculations and array operations.
  • Pandas: Climate data processing and analysis.
  • Matplotlib: Data visualization and graphs.
  • Streamlit: Interactive web dashboard.
  • NASA POWER: Source of daily climate data.
  • FAO-56 approach: Reference evapotranspiration methodology.

Creativity and design considerations:
FarmFusion combines NASA POWER climate data with an independent soil-water simulation in a location-specific agricultural dashboard. Rather than displaying climate information alone, it allows users to compare 36 scenarios involving different soil textures and initial moisture conditions. The team considered the local study area, wheat-growing period, rainfall, atmospheric water demand, soil characteristics, initial moisture assumptions, and the limitations of simplified simulation.

FarmFusion is an independent research prototype, not an official NASA product or a field-validated farming advisory system. Future development can incorporate measured local soil properties, field observations, and more detailed crop-water processes.
